scenario: [LFAC.1.7.2]: one identity, one live fact, whatever the key slot's type. A `Json` key compares by value, and an object's member order carries no meaning ([LFAC.2.5.1]). The twin of LFAC.1.7.2_bytes_key_supersedes. `Doc` is keyed on `body: Json` and carries a mutable `n`. Doc {a: 1, b: {c: 2, d: 3}} n 1 is asserted and pumped. Doc {b: {d: 3, c: 2}, a: 1} n 2 has the same members in the other order, nested one level down too, so it is the same identity with a new payload: it supersedes the first, and one Doc stays live. Doc {a: 1, b: {c: 2, d: 4}} differs in one leaf and is a second identity. Exactly 2 live facts. A key never found equal leaves 3; one compared by member order also leaves 3; one compared by shape alone, or not at all, leaves 1. runtime/LFAC.2.5.1_json_member_order pins the same equality on a schema whose only slot is the key, where a re-assert is a no-op; here the re-assert carries a new payload, so the identity must be found to supersede. PATH PINNED: the identity-key hash and equality, libds `rete/wm_rete.c` `hash_idval` and `idkey_equal` (their Json arms, through `json.c` `ds_json_deep_equal`), and the Mercury runtime's identity key over `ds.json` terms, whose members are stored sorted.
